failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Answers added unrequested corporate or entity wording, name suffixes, or attribution text instead of using the expected concise conventional form.

rejected_edits.content: When a clue names an adaptation or retelling and asks what work it is based on, return the underlying source work, not the adaptation's own title. Apply this even when the relation is implicit in the clue and made clear by context.
rejected_edits.target: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Do not mistake the described change for the requested answer.

rejected_edits.content: - When a clue quotes only the beginning of a line and asks what follows, treat it as a text-completion prompt: return the next missing word or phrase, not the title or author of the work containing the quotation.
rejected_edits.target: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
